title: Database Query - Nested Objects
description: Create a function definition for querying a database with filters, sorting, and pagination options.

scenario.context: You're building an AI agent that needs to query a user database. The agent should be able to filter results, sort them, and paginate through large datasets.
scenario.task: Define a function called 'query_database' with table name, filters (nested object), sorting, and pagination.
constraints: Optional: sort_by (object with field and order)
Optional: pagination (object with page and page_size)
scenario.example_usage: User: 'Show me active users in California, sorted by registration date' → LLM calls: query_database(table_name='users', filters={status:'active', state:'CA'}, sort_by={field:'registration_date', order:'desc'})

requirements.description: 'filters' is optional object with proper structure
'sort_by' is optional object with 'field' and 'order' properties
'pagination' is optional object with 'page' and 'page_size' properties
All nested objects have proper type definitions

hints.text: Nested objects also need their own 'type': 'object' and 'properties' definitions.
The 'sort_by.order' should use enum with values like 'asc' and 'desc'.
For 'filters', you can use additionalProperties to allow any key-value pairs, or define specific properties if you know the fields.

test_cases.name: Sort_by object with field and order
Pagination object with page and page_size

solution.explanation: This function demonstrates nested object parameters. The 'filters' object can contain any key-value pairs (using additionalProperties). The 'sort_by' object has a specific structure with 'field' and 'order' properties. The 'pagination' object contains numeric 'page' and 'page_size' fields. Only 'table_name' is required; all other parameters are optional to allow flexible querying.

common_mistakes.mistake: Not defining nested properties for objects
common_mistakes.why_wrong: Just marking something as 'type: object' without properties doesn't tell the LLM what fields to include
common_mistakes.how_to_fix: Add a 'properties' field within each object parameter defining the nested fields

common_mistakes.why_wrong: Filters, sorting, and pagination should be optional for flexibility
common_mistakes.how_to_fix: Don't include 'filters', 'sort_by', or 'pagination' in the required array

common_mistakes.mistake: Using 'integer' for page numbers instead of 'number'
common_mistakes.why_wrong: OpenAI function calling uses 'number' type for all numeric values
common_mistakes.how_to_fix: Use 'number' type for page and page_size

common_mistakes.why_wrong: Without enum constraint, the LLM might use invalid values like 'ascending' or 'up'
common_mistakes.how_to_fix: Add enum: ['asc', 'desc'] to the order field
